applicable_when: The kernel performs a layout permutation from channels-last (stride-128 in channel dim) to contiguous (NCHW). Loads use address y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1 where the x-dimension (XBLOCK=128 threads) strides by 128 floats (512 bytes) — each thread in a warp reads a different cache line, causing fully uncoalesced L1TEX loads. This saturates L2 at 96.77% and causes 44.3-cycle L1TEX stalls on 80% of scheduler cycles. The store address x2 + 31500*y3 IS contiguous in x, but the compiler cannot prove this without hints, so it emits scalar 32-bit stores instead of 128-bit vectorized stores. Adding tl.max_contiguous + tl.multiple_of on the store index and switching to autotuned XBLOCK/YBLOCK/num_warps will enable 128-bit (float4) vectorized stores and improve L2 sector efficiency.
